sentences.text: Mr. Anil Upadhyay - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/Sta Heard on I.A. No. 11701/2024, which is 3rd bail application under Section 389(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail to appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted under Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.1,000/- and Section 376(2)(N) read with Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs. 1,000/- and Section 376(3) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years and fine of Rs. 1000/- with default stipulations.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 02.08.2022 (I.A.No.4341 of 2020)
and second application was also dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 13.09.2023 (I.A.No.20357 of 2022).
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to evidence on record, submits that learned trial Court has erred in convicting and sentencing the present appellant.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
It is urged that PW-1 and PW-3 (
parents of prosecutrix) and PW-2 have turned hostile.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, after referring to the deposition of prosecutrix, it is also urged that she is not a reliable witness and from evidence on record, it is not established that on the date of incident, she was minor.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: In this connection, he has referred para 8 of deposition of father of prosecutrix.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: DNA report also does not support the prosecution story.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Further,
it is also urged that appellant is in jail since 2 CRA-9634-2019 08.06.2018.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: He has served jail sentence of almost 9 years.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: There is no possibility of early hearing of this appeal in near future
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Thus,
remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State does not dispute the factum of custody.
sentences._hearing_file: Ramdas vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, he opposed the prayer for grant of bail with support of his objection filed on record.

sentences.text: Having regard to testimonies of PW-1 to PW-5, DNA report, evidence pertaining to age of prosecutrix and also the custody period of appellant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The appellant has been convicted under Section 366 of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.1,000/- and Section 376(2)(N) read with Section 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs. 1,000/- and Section 376(3) of IPC and sentenced to undergo RI for 20 years and fine of Rs. 1000/- with default stipulations.
His first application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 02.08.2022 (I.A.No.4341 of 2020)
and second application was also dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 13.09.2023 (I.A.No.20357 of 2022).
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He has served jail sentence of almost 9 years.
However, he opposed the prayer for grant of bail with support of his objection filed on record.
opennyai_summary.final__decision:
Thus,
remaining jail sentence of appellant may be suspended.
Having regard to testimonies of PW-1 to PW-5, DNA report, evidence pertaining to age of prosecutrix and also the custody period of appellant, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of appellant.
Subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, the remaining jail sentence of the appellant-Ramdas is hereby suspended and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court with a further direction to appear before the concerning trial court on 05.03.2025 and also on such other dates, as may be fixed by the trial court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
